research_question: In adults who experienced rape or sexual assault in adulthood, what is the effect of psychosocial interventions (CBT including prolonged exposure, cognitive processing therapy and stress inoculation training; behavioural/exposure-based therapies; EMDR, memory-reconsolidation, neurofeedback or narrative exposure approaches; and brief or low-intensity interventions such as psychoeducational videos or computerised programmes), compared with an inactive control (wait-list, usual care, no treatment, assessment only), on PTSD symptom severity measured on a continuous scale immediately after treatment?
treatment_label: Psychosocial intervention (CBT/PE/CPT/SIT, exposure-based, EMDR, narrative exposure, neurofeedback, memory reconsolidation, or brief/low-intensity programmes)
control_label: Inactive control (wait-list, usual care, no treatment, or assessment only)
outcome_description: PTSD symptom severity on a continuous scale at the first post-treatment assessment (end of treatment). One measure per trial: prefer clinician-administered scales (e.g. CAPS), otherwise the trial's primary self-report PTSD scale (e.g. PDS, PCL, PSS-SR, IES-R); total scores only, not subscales. Extract mean, SD and n per arm (end-of-treatment values preferred over change scores; SE/SEM converted to SD = SE × √n). Follow-up assessments (3, 6, 12 months) are not used.
positive_direction: A positive Hedges' g means the psychosocial intervention group had LOWER PTSD symptom severity at post-treatment than the inactive control group — i.e. the effect favours the intervention (equivalent to a negative raw SMD in the user's sign convention).
search_queries: randomized controlled trial psychotherapy PTSD sexual assault rape survivors post-treatment outcome
prolonged exposure cognitive processing therapy EMDR rape victims PTSD symptoms trial wait-list
brief computerised psychoeducation intervention sexual assault PTSD severity controlled trial adults
inclusion_criteria: Randomised controlled trial in adults (18+) in which all or a substantial majority of participants experienced rape or sexual assault in adulthood
Compares any psychosocial/psychological intervention (including brief or low-intensity programmes) with an inactive control condition such as wait-list, usual care, no treatment or assessment only
Reports quantitative PTSD symptom severity data on a continuous scale at a post-treatment assessment, or statistics from which an effect size can be computed
exclusion_criteria: Not an original empirical study (systematic review, meta-analysis, editorial, commentary, opinion or purely theoretical/protocol paper)
No comparison between a treatment condition and an inactive control condition (e.g. single-arm studies, or trials whose only comparator is another active treatment, or non-randomised designs)
No quantitative outcome data permitting effect-size computation (no means with SDs/SEs, t/F values, proportions or odds ratios)
Unrelated to the research topic (e.g. samples restricted to childhood sexual abuse only, military/combat trauma without sexual assault, children or adolescents, or pharmacological interventions only)
moderators_to_extract: Intervention type (CBT/PE/CPT/SIT vs exposure-based vs EMDR/narrative/neurofeedback vs brief or low-intensity)
Control condition type (wait-list vs usual care vs no treatment/assessment only)
PTSD outcome measure type (clinician-administered vs self-report)
Number of treatment sessions / intervention intensity
effect_size_note: Pool as standardised mean difference (Hedges' g) under a random-effects model (REML, Knapp–Hartung adjustment), using post-treatment means, SDs and per-arm n. Because PTSD scales score higher = worse, effect sizes are sign-flipped so that a POSITIVE g favours the intervention (the user's convention of SMD < 0 favouring intervention is the mirror image). Multi-arm trials contribute each eligible active arm as a separate comparison against the shared inactive control, with the control n split equally across comparisons to avoid double-counting. Heterogeneity assessed with tau², I² and prediction intervals; small-study effects via funnel plot and Egger's test.
